name: License a Professional Voice Clone on the ElevenLabs Voice Library
summary: Record a high-quality voice dataset once, publish it as a Professional Voice Clone, and earn every time paid ElevenLabs users generate speech with it.
howItWorks: You record 30 min to 3 h of clean studio-quality speech and create a Professional Voice Clone (PVC), then share it in the public Voice Library with a description, tags and a notice period. Paying ElevenLabs users pick your voice for narration, ads, games and agents; ElevenLabs pays you per character generated by paid users. The work is front-loaded: after verification the voice earns with no further recording. Distinct, well-described niche voices (accents, ages, styles) earn more than generic ones.

payout.frequency: automatic every 6-8 days once threshold is met
payout.notes: Only usage by paid users counts. Payouts run automatically via Stripe Connect every 6-8 days once earnings pass the threshold ($10 in most countries). A paid plan is not required to receive payouts, but creating a Professional Voice Clone requires the Creator plan or higher.

legality.notes: Licensing your own voice is legal everywhere in the reference set; you may only clone your OWN voice (identity verification enforces this).
complianceRequirements: US tax withholding on US-customer usage

availability.notes: Depends on Stripe Connect payout support for your country; unsupported countries cannot receive payouts.

automationPlan: Agent writes the voice description, tags and use-case copy
Agent monitors the earnings dashboard and usage trends
Agent drafts promo posts/demos linking the voice (optional)
manualSteps: Record clean audio of your own voice
Buy one month of Creator plan to create the PVC
Stripe Connect KYC and bank linking
fullCycle: Auto payout to bank via Stripe
risks: Earnings concentrated in top voices; most earn little
Rates set by notice period, not by you
Your voice may be used in content you dislike (within ElevenLabs ToS)
evidence: ElevenLabs blog (May 2026, updated Sep 2026) reports voice creators have earned over $22M with 10,400+ creators paid; the official payouts help page documents the $10 threshold and 6-8 day automatic Stripe payouts.

tools: ElevenLabs Creator plan ($22/mo; first month $11, needed one month to create the PVC)
skills: basic audio recording and noise cleanup

unitEconomics.notes: Royalties are paid per character generated by paid users at ElevenLabs-set rates; figures are monthly royalties per shared voice (estimated from the $22M/10,400+ creators disclosure: heavily skewed). Platform share is already deducted. ElevenLabs does not publish per-character rates; the payout rate depends on the notice period chosen; payouts go out every 6-8 days above a ~$10 threshold.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No recurring cost after the PVC is created (a paid plan is not needed to receive payouts). Break-even is the month royalties first exceed $10.

marketConditions.notes: Distinctive niche voices (specific accents, ages, narration styles) earn most; the library now holds many thousands of voices, so generic voices get little use. Usage grows with AI audiobooks and voice agents, but ElevenLabs controls rates and discovery. Failure mode: a technically fine voice that ranks low and earns a few dollars a month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: You do not set prices directly; choose a longer notice period (higher rate tier) only if your voice is distinctive, and optimise the description and sample for discovery.
profitPath: Month 0: record 1-3 hours, create and verify PVC, share in library (cost $22)
Month 1-2: first royalties; $0-$20
Month 3-6: refine description/samples, add a second style; $5-$50/month
Month 6-12: passive royalties; $15 median, $100+ for distinctive voices

name: Sell labeled AI-generated stock images, vectors and video on Adobe Stock and Freepik
summary: Generate commercially-useful stock assets with image/video models and license them on the few major agencies that explicitly accept labeled generative-AI content.
howItWorks: Adobe Stock and Freepik accept generative-AI submissions if they are labeled as AI, contain no real people/brands/artist names, and meet quality rules. An agent can research high-demand gaps (search trends, seasonal themes), generate batches, upscale, write titles/keywords and upload via FTP/CSV. Buyers (designers, marketers) license assets; you receive a royalty per download. Volume and keyword quality drive income; acceptance rates for AI content are strict.

payout.minimumPayout: Adobe Stock $25 (first payout only after 45 days since first sale); Freepik/Magnific $25 / EUR 50
payout.notes: Adobe: request payout once $25 is reached; PayPal global, Payoneer outside the US, Skrill most countries. Freepik's contributor program now runs under the Magnific brand: pay-per-download from subscriber revenue, invoices generated 2 months after the minimum is reached, paid between the 10th and 15th. New Freepik/Magnific contributors must pass a 150-200 asset first review.

legality.notes: Legal; must tick 'Created using generative AI tools', avoid real persons/trademarks/copyrighted characters and artist names in prompts.
complianceRequirements: generator ToS must grant commercial rights

availability.notes: Adobe Stock contributors worldwide with PayPal/Skrill; Freepik via PayPal/Payoneer, which cover most reference countries.

automationPlan: Agent mines trending/under-supplied search terms
Batch generation + upscaling pipeline
LLM-generated titles and 25-49 keywords per asset
CSV/FTP upload and rejection-reason analysis
manualSteps: Create contributor accounts and pass ID check
Spot-check quality and IP risk before upload
risks: Market flooded with AI images; per-download revenue falling
High rejection rates, possible account limits for spammy volume
Policy can change (Shutterstock/Getty already reject AI content)
evidence: Freepik reports 42,000+ contributors publishing 7.5M AI images; Adobe maintains dedicated generative-AI submission guidelines (updated 2026).

tools: image generator subscription (~$10/mo, e.g. Midjourney Basic or Firefly credits)
Adobe Stock Contributor and Freepik/Magnific contributor (free)
accounts: Adobe Stock Contributor account + tax form

unitEconomics.notes: Contributor royalties average roughly $0.10-$1.50 per download (Adobe pays a 33% royalty; Freepik pays cents per download from a subscription pool); price is your royalty, so the platform share is already deducted. Cost = generation credits per batch (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). ~100 downloads/month covers the generator subscription, which usually needs a portfolio of 1,000-3,000 accepted assets.

marketConditions.notes: Large-volume contributors with sharp keywording and seasonal planning earn; Freepik alone reports millions of AI images from 42,000+ contributors. Buyers increasingly generate images themselves inside Adobe and Freepik tools, pushing per-download royalties down. Failure mode: high rejection rates and portfolios that earn cents per day.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No price control; win by filling search gaps (business concepts, seasonal, diverse authentic scenes) and uploading consistently, and by adding vectors/video, which earn more per download.
profitPath: Month 0: set up accounts, generate first 200 assets (cost $10/mo)
Month 1-2: pass reviews, first downloads; $0-$10
Month 3-6: scale to 1,000+ assets with an agent pipeline; $10-$40/month
Month 6-12: focus on top-selling themes, add video; $15-$200/month

name: Build monetized bots on Poe (per-message pricing)
summary: Publish AI bots on Quora's Poe, set a per-message price, and get paid by Poe for every message your bot answers.
howItWorks: Poe hosts thousands of bots built on frontier models. Creators build prompt bots or server bots (your own code via the Poe API) that solve a specific job: e.g. a specialized converter, tutor or image workflow. You join creator monetization at poe.com/creators and set a price per message (up to $10,000 per 1,000 messages); Poe pays you that price for each message your bot responds to. An agent can build, test and iterate server bots, write descriptions, and track usage. Earnings depend on discovery inside Poe.

payout.notes: Taxpayer info must be submitted within 90 days of joining. Eligible regions (official FAQ): Argentina, Australia, Belgium, Canada, Colombia, Denmark, Finland, Germany, Hong Kong, India, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Mexico, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, UK, US. The current FAQ describes only per-message earnings (no subscription-referral share).

legality.notes: Legal; bots must follow Poe and underlying-model usage policies.

availability.notes: Only 23 eligible regions; of the reference countries just 12 qualify (US, Canada, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, Australia, Argentina, Colombia, Mexico, India, Singapore) = ~24%.

automationPlan: Agent builds server bots via Poe API and fastapi-poe
Auto-generate descriptions/sample prompts
Monitor usage and adjust per-message price
A/B test bot variants
risks: Underlying model costs can eat margin for server bots
evidence: Poe's official Creator Monetization FAQ documents per-message pricing, Stripe payouts, the $10 threshold and the 23-region eligibility list; Quora raised $75M from a16z largely to fund creator payouts.

tools: server bot hosting (~$5/mo, e.g. Modal/Fly free-to-low tiers)
LLM API credits for server bots
skills: Python for server bots (AI coding agent covers most)
accounts: Stripe account + tax info within 90 days

unitEconomics.notes: Creators set the per-message price; a few dollars to tens of dollars per 1,000 messages is common for useful bots (estimate). Cost = model/API usage for server bots; prompt bots cost $0. Poe's earnings terms confirm creators set a per-message price but publish no rate or fee.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost is server hosting only; one median block of 1,000 messages covers it.

marketConditions.notes: A handful of specialised bots with retained users earn; most get no discovery. Poe has changed creator terms several times (the current FAQ lists only per-message earnings), and frontier chat apps now offer agents and apps that overlap with bots. Failure mode: no traffic, or API costs above earnings for server bots.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start below competing bots' per-message price to attract usage, then raise for power users once the bot shows retention; never price below your model cost per message.
profitPath: Month 0: build 2-3 bots including one server bot (cost $0-$5/mo)
Month 1-2: iterate; $0-$10
Month 3-6: improve the bot with retention; $5-$50/month
Month 6-12: port the winner to other channels; $5-$300/month

name: AI dubbing and subtitle localization service for creators and course sellers
summary: Sell AI-powered dubbing, subtitles and translated thumbnails/descriptions to YouTubers, course creators and SaaS companies who want new language markets.
howItWorks: Many creators can reach 2-5x more viewers with dubbed audio tracks (YouTube supports multi-language audio). You run their video through AI transcription, translation, voice cloning (with their consent) and lip-sync tools, then a native-speaker check where needed, and deliver files or upload to their channel. Clients pay per minute or a monthly retainer. An agent handles the whole pipeline; humans sell and QA.

payout.notes: Pricing is set by you; $1-$10 per finished minute per language is a rough market estimate, not an official benchmark (unverified).

legality.notes: Legal; only clone voices with written consent of the voice owner and only localize content the client owns.
complianceRequirements: data processing agreement for EU clients

availability.notes: Direct invoicing works almost everywhere via Wise/Payoneer/PayPal.

automationPlan: Agent: transcribe -> translate -> dub -> subtitle pipeline
Auto QA (timing, glossary consistency)
Agent drafts outreach and proposals
Auto-upload multi-language tracks via YouTube API with client OAuth
risks: Tool vendors (YouTube auto-dubbing) commoditize basic service
evidence: YouTube's multi-language audio and ElevenLabs dubbing are widely used by large channels to expand reach; agencies sell this service publicly.

tools: ElevenLabs Creator ($22/mo, $11 first month; Pro $99/mo as volume grows)
skills: quality control in at least one target language (or a paid native reviewer)

unitEconomics.notes: Self-set pricing; $1-$10 per minute per language is an estimated market range, premium lip-sync up to ~$15. Cost = AI credits (ElevenLabs automatic dubbing without watermark uses 3,000 credits per minute; ~$1/min with retries, estimated); fee = payment processing.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). About 7 finished minutes a month cover the tool subscription.

marketConditions.notes: Agencies that bundle dubbing with channel strategy and native-speaker QA retain clients; plain dubbing is being commoditised by YouTube's built-in auto-dubbing (expanded across the Partner Program in 2025) and self-serve tools. Course sellers and B2B video still pay for quality. Failure mode: competing on price against free platform features and losing clients to bad translations. Median net at month 12 set to $60 to match the 25% profit likelihood.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Offer a free 3-minute pilot, then a monthly retainer per language (e.g. 4 videos/month); raise prices once you show view-growth case studies.
profitPath: Month 0: build pipeline, dub 3 sample videos, portfolio page (cost $50 + $22/mo)
Month 1-2: outreach to 100 creators; first client $50-$300
Month 3-6: 2-4 retainer clients; $200-$800/month
Month 6-12: add languages and a native reviewer; $150 median, $1,000+ top quartile

name: Niche 'AI employee' chatbot/voice agent sold per seat to a vertical
summary: Build a no-code AI agent (Voiceflow/Botpress) for one vertical (e.g. dental clinics, property managers) and sell it as a monthly subscription.
howItWorks: You pick a vertical with repetitive inbound questions or bookings, build an agent connected to their calendar/CRM/FAQ, and resell it as a done-for-you monthly service. Clients pay a setup fee plus per-seat or per-location monthly. Botpress has a formal partner program for agencies; Voiceflow targets agencies. Once one template works, cloning it for new clients is largely automated; sales remains human.

payout.notes: Common pricing $99-$500/month per client plus setup.

legality.notes: Legal; respect call-recording/consent and AI-disclosure rules (e.g. EU AI Act transparency, US state bot-disclosure laws, TCPA for outbound calls).

availability.notes: Tooling available globally; billing via Stripe or Wise/Payoneer invoices.

automationPlan: Template agent cloned per client via API
Agent ingests client docs into knowledge base
Automated conversation QA and reports
Billing automation via Stripe
risks: Churn when vertical SaaS adds native AI
evidence: Botpress runs an official partner program for agencies selling AI agents as a service; many agencies publicly sell AI receptionists per month.

tools: Botpress (free tier to start; Plus $150/mo billed annually once clients pay for it) or Voiceflow (usage-based)

unitEconomics.notes: Agencies commonly charge $99-$500/month per location plus setup; cost = LLM/voice usage per client (estimate); fee = card processing.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). One client covers platform fees; setup fees often cover the startup cash. Fixed cost assumes the free/usage-based builder tier plus voice/LLM floor; upgrading to Botpress Plus adds ~$150/mo (estimated as a pass-through to clients).

marketConditions.notes: The 'AI automation agency' wave of 2024-2026 made this crowded; winners specialise in one vertical (dental, HVAC, real estate) and own a referral channel. Vertical SaaS vendors increasingly bundle native AI receptionists, pressuring prices. Failure mode: no sales skills, or churn after a hallucination incident. Median net at month 12 set to $80 to match the 20% profit likelihood.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Charge a setup fee ($300-$1,000) plus a monthly fee with a 30-day pilot; raise prices after documenting booked appointments or saved staff hours.
profitPath: Month 0: build a vertical demo agent (cost $50 + $50/mo)
Month 1-2: 100+ outreach contacts, 1 pilot; $0-$300
Month 3-6: 2-3 paying clients; $250-$750/month
Month 6-12: templated onboarding, 4-10 clients; $300 median, $2,000+ top quartile

name: Premium AI Discord bot via Discord App Subscriptions
summary: Build a useful AI-powered Discord bot (moderation, summaries, game master, translation) and sell premium tiers natively in Discord.
howItWorks: Discord lets verified apps sell subscriptions and one-time SKUs inside Discord. An AI bot that summarizes channels, translates, moderates or runs games can charge per server or per user. Coding agents can build and maintain the bot; usage costs (LLM API) must be below the subscription price. Discord pays out via Stripe after a monetization eligibility review.

payout.minimumPayout: $100 earned for first payout (after a manual eligibility review); $25 thereafter
payout.frequency: monthly, within 45 days after month end
payout.notes: Developers keep 85% (15% platform fee) on the first $1M cumulative gross sales, then 70%, less processing fees. Payouts are not automatic: Developer Support runs a payout eligibility review first. Native Premium Apps only for teams based in the US, UK or EU; others need external billing where Discord policy allows.

legality.notes: Legal; must follow Discord Developer Policy (no data selling, privacy policy required, no message logging beyond need).

availability.notes: Native Premium Apps limited to US/UK/EU-based developers: of the reference countries only US, UK, Germany, France, Italy, Estonia and Hungary = 14%.

automationPlan: Coding agent builds and deploys bot
Auto-scaling hosting and cost monitoring
Agent writes listing copy for Top.gg
Automated support FAQ
evidence: Discord's official 'Premium Apps Payout' article documents Stripe payouts, the $100/$25 thresholds, 45-day timing and the 85/15 split.

skills: LLM cost control and rate limiting
accounts: Discord developer team (US/UK/EU-based for native Premium Apps)
Stripe account via Discord monetization onboarding

unitEconomics.notes: Premium bot subscriptions typically cost $3-$10/month per server or user; Discord's 15% share (30% above $1M cumulative sales) is per its Premium Apps Payout article, as in payout notes; cost = LLM usage plus processing (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). About 7 median subscribers cover hosting and API floor; first payout additionally needs $100 earned and a manual review.

marketConditions.notes: Bots with a strong community niche (game servers, translation, moderation) convert; generic AI chat bots compete with free bots and Discord's own features. Native monetization is only for US/UK/EU teams, limiting eligibility to ~14% of reference countries. Failure mode: LLM costs outpace subscriptions, or installs never convert.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Free tier with daily limits, $3-$5 server subscription for higher limits; add higher tiers for large servers once usage data shows heavy users.
profitPath: Month 0: build bot, apply for monetization (cost $20)
Month 1-2: list on Top.gg; $0-$10
Month 3-6: 10-30 subscribers; $20-$100/month
Month 6-12: tune costs, upsell big servers; $15 median net

name: Authorized AI red-teaming competitions and model safety bug bounties
summary: Earn prizes and bounties by finding jailbreaks and prompt-injection vulnerabilities in authorized programs (Gray Swan Arena challenges, Anthropic's invite-only model safety bounty on HackerOne).
howItWorks: AI labs and Gray Swan run sanctioned challenges where breaking the model's safeguards is the goal. Gray Swan Arena runs free, time-bound prize challenges (e.g. a $300K indirect prompt-injection wave in Nov 2026) and splits each pool across the leaderboard; Anthropic runs an ongoing, application/invite-only model safety bounty on HackerOne paying up to $35K per novel universal jailbreak. OpenAI's Bugcrowd bounty pays for product security bugs only; jailbreaks and model-behavior issues are explicitly out of scope. AI agents can help generate and test attack variants within each program's rules. Only participate in authorized scopes; never publish or misuse harmful outputs.

methods: Gray Swan prize transfer (method per winner onboarding)
payout.minimumPayout: HackerOne: none beyond method minimums; Gray Swan: prize amount
payout.frequency: per accepted report / after challenge wave ends
payout.notes: Gray Swan states $1M+ rewards paid to 15K+ red-teamers; Anthropic pays up to $35K per novel universal jailbreak (invite via application, NDA). Gray Swan's prize payout method was not verifiable from public pages.

legality.notes: Legal only within program scope and rules; out-of-scope probing can violate ToS/computer misuse laws.

availability.notes: Global except sanctioned countries; some programs invite-only.

automationPlan: Agent generates and logs attack variants within scope
Automated scoring/replay against provided aliases
Agent drafts reports
evidence: Gray Swan Arena homepage (Nov 2026) shows $1M+ rewards paid, 15K+ red-teamers and a live $300K pool; Anthropic's help article (Sep 2026) describes the ongoing HackerOne program. OpenAI's Bugcrowd policy explicitly excludes jailbreaks, so it is not a payout path for this strategy.

accounts: Gray Swan Arena account + KYC for prizes

unitEconomics.notes: Arena leaderboard prizes for most winners are tens to hundreds of dollars; top universal jailbreaks in invite-only programs pay up to $35K (estimate of distribution). Arena page rate-limited at check time; prize distribution not verified.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No costs; break-even is the first prize, which most participants never receive.

marketConditions.notes: A small group of skilled red-teamers takes most prizes; competitions attract thousands of participants. Labs expanded safety testing in 2025-2026, but invite-only programs require a track record. Failure mode: many hours with no leaderboard placement.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not price-set; focus on early waves of new challenges, document findings thoroughly, and use a public record to apply to invite-only programs.
profitPath: Month 0: join Arena and read rules (cost $0)
Month 1-3: compete in 2-3 waves; $0-$100
Month 3-6: specialise in one attack class; $0-$300
Month 6-12: apply to invite-only programs; $0 median, $1,500 top

name: Train and publish SFW LoRA/fine-tuned image models on Tensor.Art creator incentives
summary: Train specialized style/concept LoRAs and earn daily creator incentives when other users run them on Tensor.Art.
howItWorks: Model-hosting platforms pay creators when their models are used in online generation. Tensor.Art restructured its creator incentives in July 2026 (TenStar Fund, Pro Model and Pro Tools incentives) with daily earnings updates. You train LoRAs on data you own or that is licensed (your own art, CC0, your photos), publish them with clear license terms, and keep them SFW. Agents can curate datasets, caption, train and publish variants.

payout.frequency: earnings credited daily (TensorArt) / weekly Monday (TensorHub); withdrawals processed weekly, usually Mondays
payout.notes: TensorHub pays all original public models automatically (no application). Since 22 Jul 2026 the main TensorArt site only pays incentives on Pro-user usage of approved Pro models/tools or designated new base models, and creators report sharply lower rates. Per-run rates are not published.

legality.notes: Legal if training data is owned/licensed and no real-person likeness or copyrighted characters are used; keep SFW to satisfy this catalog's rules.

availability.notes: Platform reachable in most countries; withdrawals go to a bank account entered at withdrawal time, but the list of supported payout countries is not published (unverified).

automationPlan: Agent curates and captions datasets
Automated training runs on cloud GPU
Agent writes model cards and sample images
Track runs and iterate popular styles
evidence: Tensor.Art's official TensorHub Creator Incentive notice (Feb 2026) documents automatic enrollment, weekly Monday payouts and the $50 withdrawal minimum; a Jul 2026 notice restructured TensorArt incentives.

tools: online LoRA trainer credits or a local GPU
skills: writing model cards and license terms
equipment: optional GPU (8 GB+ VRAM) or cloud credits

Cost = training compute amortised per model-month. Tensor.Art articles bot-blocked at check time; the July 2026 cut is unverified.

name: License your unused video/footage archive as AI training data
summary: Sell rights to raw or unpublished video you own to AI companies through data brokers like Troveo, who pay per minute.
howItWorks: AI video model labs buy licensed footage; brokers (Troveo, Calliope Networks) aggregate creator archives and pay roughly $1-$4 per minute depending on quality and format. You must own the footage and have releases for identifiable people. An agent can inventory and tag archives, strip unwanted segments, prepare metadata and handle uploads. One-off or recurring payments as new footage is added.

payout.frequency: per licensing deal; no fixed schedule
payout.notes: Troveo pays only after your content is licensed, the AI client is invoiced and pays; non-US licensors submit W-8BEN. Troveo does not publish per-minute rates; the ~$1-$4/minute range comes from press reports.

legality.notes: Legal if you own copyright and have releases; check that footage doesn't include others' likenesses or copyrighted music.
complianceRequirements: privacy law for people in footage

availability.notes: Troveo pays international licensors via Tipalti bank transfer; exact country list not published.

automationPlan: Agent catalogs archive and computes minutes by category
Automated de-duplication and quality filtering
Metadata generation
Upload automation
risks: Prices may fall as supply grows
evidence: Troveo's content-owner page states $50M+ paid to creators globally; Bloomberg (Jan 2025) reported YouTubers selling unused footage to AI firms.

unitEconomics.notes: Press reports cite ~$1-$4 per minute paid to creators; brokers do not publish rates; prices shown are net to creator (estimate). Troveo's payout article confirms payment only when footage is licensed, with no fixed schedule and no published rate.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No costs; payment arrives only after a lab licenses the footage.

marketConditions.notes: People with large archives of owned, release-cleared footage (B-roll, drone, nature) are paid; Troveo reports $50M+ paid. Supply is rising and synthetic data may reduce prices. Failure mode: no archive, or content rejected over releases/quality.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not price-set; prioritise high-value formats (4K, drone, unusual locations) and negotiate non-exclusive licences.
profitPath: Month 0: inventory archive (cost $0)
Month 1-2: submit; $0

name: Free AI-powered micro-tools website monetized by display ads and freemium
summary: A site of single-purpose AI tools (e.g. 'rewrite email in formal tone', 'generate alt text', 'CSV to chart') that captures search traffic and earns from ads and premium usage.
howItWorks: Each tool page targets a search query with real utility (not thin content). LLM APIs do the work; free usage is rate-limited, and a cheap subscription unlocks more. Revenue from display ads (AdSense, later Ezoic/Mediavine-type networks) and Stripe subscriptions. Coding agents can build new tools quickly from a template and monitor which pages rank.

payout.notes: API costs must stay below ad + subscription revenue per user.

legality.notes: Legal; follow AdSense policies (no auto-generated thin pages, no invalid traffic) and Google spam policies on scaled content.

availability.notes: AdSense pays in nearly all reference countries; Stripe for subscriptions where supported, else Paddle/Lemon Squeezy.
